tagline: Down Bishop Creek from a power lake to the Owens Valley.
intro: Highway 168 begins at Lake Sabrina, high on the eastern slope of the Sierra Nevada, and follows Bishop Creek down past Aspendell, at 8,409 feet, to Bishop at 4,150 feet in the Owens Valley. Below Intake Two the forks of the creek have come together, and it starts its steep descent.

The road was meant to keep going west. The state once planned a High Sierra Piute Highway over 11,453-foot Piute Pass to Fresno. The crest and two wilderness areas stood in the way, and the gap is still crossed on foot.

moments.title: Lake Sabrina
moments.text: Dammed in 1907 and 1908 to keep water running to the power plants, and named for Sabrina Hobbs, wife of the power company's manager. Locals pronounce it differently than she did.

moments.title: Aspendell
moments.text: A village of about 70, laid out in 1961 and known in fall for its aspens. Its lone resort began in a mining town born of an 1885 gold strike on the creek.

moments.title: Bishop
moments.text: The valley town took its name from the creek, and the creek from Samuel Addison Bishop, an early settler. John Wayne made westerns here.

practical: The road from Aspendell up to Lake Sabrina is closed to most vehicles in winter, usually until mid- or late April; the gate is just southwest of Aspendell.
